clues: This town is the chief town of its land, built by plan in the 1960s by the green hills. It took the chief town's seat from the great port town.
This town counts five times of year, not four: the fifth is the Rainy Monsoon of July and August. July storms can burst in a flash and flood the streets.
A Greek plan-maker drew this town's great plan from scratch. He split it into eight zones, each with its own work to do.
The land's flag-ship mosque stands in this town, a vast white tent of stone. It is the town's crown sight, seen from far off.
Wild park land fills much of this town: a whole state park lies in its bounds. Green hills watch over its straight streets.
